description: Technical specification for normalizing the knowledge graph schema across all node types, validating cross-references, and ensuring code can parse every file consistently.

canonical_concept_schema.description: Every concept node, regardless of category, MUST have these fields. Implementation should validate at load time.

required_fields.id: string — unique identifier, snake_case, used for cross-references
required_fields.name: string — human-readable display name
required_fields.category: string — one of: archetype, process, structure, typology
required_fields.plain_language: string — from accessibility overlay. The version for someone who's never read Jung
required_fields.relationships: array of { target: string (concept ID), type: string (relationship type), note: string }

optional_fields.in_practice: string — what this looks like in lived experience
optional_fields.recognition_patterns: array of strings — how to recognize this in dreams or life
optional_fields.jung_sources: array of { work: string, year: integer, public_domain: boolean, note?: string }
optional_fields.assessment_signals: array of strings — indicators for the assessment framework
optional_fields.activation_indicators: string — when this archetype/process is most active
optional_fields.contemporary_note: string — how contemporary practice differs from Jung's original
optional_fields.contested: object or null — { issue: string, positions: array, graph_position: string }
optional_fields.first_encounter_phrase: string or null — from accessibility overlay
optional_fields.app_relevance: string — how this concept serves the app specifically
optional_fields.subcategory: string — for further classification within category
optional_fields.variations: array — for symbols with multiple forms

required_fields.name: string — human-readable display name
required_fields.category: string — one of: element, space, figure, creature, object, action, body, transition, color, number, scenario, atmosphere
required_fields.recognition_terms: array of strings — words/phrases that trigger this symbol's detection in transcripts

optional_fields.variations: array of { form: string, meaning: string, intensity: string (low/medium/high) }
optional_fields.dream_context_clues: array of strings — guidance for contextual interpretation
optional_fields.app_response_guidance: object — specific guidance for the LLM when this symbol appears

required_fields.framework_elements: array of { framework: string (framework ID), stage: string (stage ID) }
required_fields.mapping_type: string — one of: parallel, sequence, contains, tension, metaphor
required_fields.strength: string — one of: strong, moderate, suggestive
required_fields.in_dreams: string — how this mapping manifests in dream content

relationship_types.description: All relationship 'type' fields must use one of these values. Any other value should be flagged during validation.

cross_reference_manifest.description: Every ID referenced anywhere in the knowledge graph must resolve to an actual node. This manifest lists all valid IDs for validation.
validation_rules: Every 'target' in a relationship must exist in concept_ids
Every entry in 'jungian_concepts' on symbols must exist in concept_ids
Every 'framework' in bridge elements must exist in framework_ids
Every 'stage' in bridge elements must exist within the referenced framework's stage list
Every entry in 'related_symbols' should resolve to a symbol ID (cross-file validation)
Every 'keyed_to' in integration practices should resolve to a concept ID

file_merge_order.description: When loading the knowledge graph, files should be merged in this order to ensure all references resolve.
order: 2. All concepts-batch-*.json — merged into a single concepts map
4. All symbols*.json — merged into a single symbols map
7. bridge.json + bridge-expanded.json — merged into a single bridge map
10. All methodology documents (dream-analysis-protocol, dream-series-protocol, integration-practices, therapeutic-boundaries)
13. living-system.json (system prompt, onboarding, voice library, incubation)

implementation_notes: The accessibility overlay files add fields to existing nodes — they don't replace them. Merge by ID.
For LLM context injection, the system prompt should load first, then only the RELEVANT concept and symbol nodes for the specific dream being analyzed — not the entire graph.
The depth_tier field controls progressive disclosure: only introduce tier-2 and tier-3 concepts when the user has demonstrated readiness (entry count, direct questions, or explicit curiosity).
Contested fields should trigger the LLM to present the concept with appropriate tentativeness: 'Some practitioners see this differently...'
The voice library in living-system.json should be loaded alongside the system prompt — it governs HOW the LLM speaks, not WHAT it knows.
